content:
Google Ads can bring a Gurugram business enquiries on the same day a campaign goes live. It can also spend a month's budget on clicks from students, job seekers and people in the wrong city. The difference is almost always in the setup: what is tracked, which searches you pay for, where the ads show and what happens after the click.

We manage Google Ads for businesses from our office on Sohna Road in Sector 49. Here is how we run accounts and what you should expect from any agency handling your ad spend.

Start With Tracking, Not Keywords

Before a single keyword is added, we make sure every valuable action is measured. Without this, Google's automated bidding optimizes for clicks instead of customers, and nobody can tell which campaign is working.

  • Form submissions tracked through Google Ads conversion tracking and Google Tag Manager, firing only on a real thank-you page or confirmed submit
  • Phone calls from ads and from the website, with a minimum call length so misdials do not count as leads
  • WhatsApp clicks, since many Gurugram customers prefer to message rather than call or fill a form
  • GA4 linked to Google Ads so you can see how ad visitors behave on the site
  • Offline conversion import (where your CRM or lead sheet allows it) so Google learns which leads turned into site visits, admissions or sales

The last point matters for real estate, education and healthcare, where many form fills never pick up the phone. Feeding back which leads were genuine helps the bidding system find more people like them.

How We Build a Campaign

  1. Search intent research: we list the searches a real buyer types, from "physiotherapy clinic near me" to "3 BHK Dwarka Expressway ready to move", and separate them from research or job-hunting searches. Many people still type "Gurgaon" instead of Gurugram, so both spellings go into the keyword list.
  2. Negative keywords: we block terms like "jobs", "salary", "course", "free", "PDF" and competitor-irrelevant searches from day one, then keep adding from the search terms report.
  3. Location targeting: we target the areas you actually serve, by radius around your location or by selected pincodes and areas, and set it to people located in those areas rather than people merely interested in them.
  4. Ad copy and assets: ads that mention specifics such as the locality, timings, parking, or a same-day slot, with sitelinks, callouts and call assets.
  5. Landing page: a focused page for each offer, loading fast on mobile, with a short form, a call button and a WhatsApp button. Sending ad traffic to a busy homepage wastes money.
  6. Launch and learning: we start with controlled bids, watch search terms daily for the first two weeks, and move to automated bidding only once enough conversions are recorded.

A typical setup, from access to live campaigns, takes one to two weeks. The first four to six weeks after launch are a learning period in which we cut waste and refine targeting.

Campaign Types We Use, and When

  • Search campaigns
  • Performance Max
  • Call ads
  • YouTube video campaigns
  • Display remarketing
  • Demand Gen

For most local service businesses, Search campaigns do the heavy lifting because they catch people who are ready to act. Performance Max can work well for businesses with good conversion data and strong creative, but it needs tight tracking and exclusions or it tends to drift towards cheap, low-quality placements. YouTube and Demand Gen help with launches and real estate projects where people need to see the product before enquiring.

What Drives Your Monthly Cost

There are two separate costs: the ad spend you pay Google directly, and our management fee. Ad spend depends on how competitive your searches are (legal, real estate and some healthcare terms cost much more per click than, say, a cafe), how many areas you target and how many enquiries you want. Our fee depends on the number of campaigns, landing pages and tracking work involved. After a free account audit or discovery call, we give a fixed quote and a recommended starting budget with reasoning, not a figure picked to look attractive.

Signs Your Current Account Is Leaking Money

  • Broad match keywords with no negative keyword list
  • Location set to "presence or interest", showing ads to people outside Gurugram
  • Conversions counting page views or button clicks instead of real enquiries
  • All keywords in one ad group with one generic ad
  • Auto-applied recommendations switched on without anyone reviewing them
  • No one has looked at the search terms report in weeks
  • The agency owns the ad account, not you

The last point is important. The Google Ads account should be created under your business and you should keep admin access. We work as managers on your account, so the data and history stay with you if you ever change agencies.

What You Need to Give Us

  • Admin access to your Google Ads account, or a billing profile so we can create one in your name
  • Access to the website or a developer who can add tracking
  • Your service areas, working hours and how quickly the team can respond to leads
  • Honest feedback on lead quality every week, at least in the first month

Who Should Not Run Google Ads Yet

Paid search is hard to make profitable if nobody answers the phone during ad hours, if the website does not work on mobile, or if the average sale is too small to cover the cost of a click and follow-up. It is also a weak fit for products nobody is searching for yet; a new category often needs awareness through social media first.

Google Ads Questions From Business Owners

How soon will we get leads?

Search ads can bring enquiries within the first few days of going live. Lead quality and cost per lead usually improve over the first four to six weeks as we add negatives and the bidding system learns.

Can we show ads only in specific sectors?

Yes, within limits. Google lets us target a radius around a point or specific postal areas. It cannot target individual sectors perfectly, but a clinic on Sohna Road can target nearby areas rather than the whole of Gurugram or Delhi NCR.

Why do we get so many irrelevant leads?

Usually because of broad keywords, missing negatives, weak form questions or Performance Max running without exclusions. A short account audit normally shows the cause.

Who pays Google?

You do, directly, using your own card or invoice billing. Our management fee is billed separately, so you always see exactly what went to Google.

Do we need a new website?

Not always. Often one or two dedicated landing pages are enough. We will tell you after reviewing your site.
